chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), that he said:

Love your Muslim brother, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. When you are in need, ask him, and when he asks you, give to him. Do not withhold goodness from him, for indeed he does not withhold it from you.

Be a support for him, for indeed he is a support for you. If he is absent, protect him in his absence, and if he is present, visit him. Honour him and be generous to him, for he is from you and you are from him.

If he reproaches you, do not part from him until you draw out his grudge and what is in his heart. When good befalls him, praise God for it, and if he is afflicted, support him and share in his burden.

key_terms.تمحل: Tamahhal - to strive on behalf of another, to share their burden and seek solutions for them
key_terms.سخيمة: Sakhimah - grudge, rancour, deep-seated resentment in the heart
key_terms.ظهر: Zahr - literally 'back'; metaphorically a supporter, one who has your back

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a Muslim brother according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) delivered this comprehensive teaching on the rights of Muslim brotherhood to his companions, outlining the reciprocal duties believers owe one another. The teaching covers emotional solidarity (loving and disliking the same things for one's brother), material generosity (mutual giving without reservation), loyalty (being a steadfast support and protector in absence), social courtesy (visiting, honouring, and showing generosity), conflict resolution (not parting until rancour is resolved), and empathy in both prosperity and adversity.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Safwan b. Yahya from al-`Is b. al-Qasim from `Abdullah b. Muskan from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as). He said:

Love your Muslim brother. Love for him what you love for yourself. Hate for him what you hate for yourself. If you need something, ask him for it, and if he asks you, then give to him. Do not spare him from goodness as he does not spare you from goodness.
Be a back to him as he is a back to you. When he goes, then protect [his belongings] in his absence. When he is present, visit him. Honour him, for he is from you and you are from him.

If he blames you, then do not depart from him until you seek his forgiveness and [ask him to speak] his mind. If a good thing happens to him, then praise Allah for it, and if he suffers, then support him and share in his burden.
